entries.title: James 2:1
segments: The Lord of glory. In the presence of the very Lord of glory, how utterly vain and foolish appear the honors conferred through respect of persons.

entries.title: James 2:2
segments: A man with a gold ring. This was a fashion borrowed from the luxurious Romans, and aping their vanity and self-importance.

entries.title: James 2:5
segments: Poor as to the world. The phrase means more than the mere accident of temporal poverty.  It relates rather to indifferences as to worldly possessions, and is qualified by the final words of the verse; 'them that love him.'

entries.title: James 2:16
segments: Be ye warmed and filled; and yet ye give them not the things needful. This is a condemnation of the prayer of mere words, which stops short of the practical, effectual prayer expressed in deeds.

entries.title: James 2:21
segments: Was not Abraham our father justified by works? Compare
